Laravel

Complete Artisan Command Reference & Concept Guide v13.x PHP 8.3+ Released Mar 17, 2026

Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax. This guide covers all Artisan commands, core concepts, and practical code examples for Laravel 13.x — including new PHP Attributes, AI SDK, and Passkey authentication.

Installation

# Create a new Laravel 13 application

composer create-project laravel/laravel myapp

# Or via the Laravel installer

laravel new myapp

# Start the development server

php artisan serve

# Start with Laravel Sail (Docker)

./vendor/bin/sail up

# Install common packages

composer require laravel/breeze   # Auth scaffolding
composer require laravel/horizon  # Queue dashboard
composer require laravel/sanctum  # API tokens
composer require laravel/pennant  # Feature flags
composer require laravel/pint     # Code style fixer

Artisan Commands Reference

All commands are run via php artisan <command> from the application root. Laravel 13 ships with 257+ built-in commands.

Routing

Define routes in routes/web.php (web) and routes/api.php (API).

routes/web.php — Examples
// Basic GET route

Route::get('/articles', [ArticleController::class, 'index']);

// Named route

Route::get('/articles/{slug}', [ArticleController::class, 'view'])
    ->name('articles.show');

// Route with parameters

Route::get('/user/{id}', function (string $id) {
    return 'User '.$id;
})->where('id', '[0-9]+');

// Route groups with middleware

Route::middleware(['auth'])->group(function () {
    Route::get('/dashboard', [DashboardController::class, 'index']);
    Route::resource('articles', ArticleController::class);
});

// Resourceful routes

Route::resource('articles', ArticleController::class);
// Generates: index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy


// API resource (no create/edit views)

Route::apiResource('articles', ArticleController::class);

// Nested resource

Route::resource('articles.comments', CommentController::class);

// Route with prefix

Route::prefix('admin')->group(function () {
    Route::get('/users', [AdminController::class, 'users']);
});

Controllers

ArticleController — Resource Full CRUD
namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Article;
use App\Http\Requests\StoreArticleRequest;
use App\Http\Requests\UpdateArticleRequest;
use Illuminate\Http\RedirectResponse;
use Illuminate\View\View;

class ArticleController extends Controller
{
    public function index(): View
    {
        $articles = Article::with('author', 'tags')
            ->latest()
            ->paginate(20);
        return view('articles.index', compact('articles'));
    }

    public function create(): View
    {
        return view('articles.create');
    }

    public function store(StoreArticleRequest $request): RedirectResponse
    {
        $article = auth()->user()->articles()
            ->create($request->validated());
        return redirect()->route('articles.show', $article)
            ->with('success', 'Article created.');
    }

    public function show(Article $article): View
    {
        return view('articles.show', compact('article'));
    }

    public function edit(Article $article): View
    {
        return view('articles.edit', compact('article'));
    }

    public function update(UpdateArticleRequest $request, Article $article): RedirectResponse
    {
        $article->update($request->validated());
        return redirect()->route('articles.show', $article)
            ->with('success', 'Article updated.');
    }

    public function destroy(Article $article): RedirectResponse
    {
        $article->delete();
        return redirect()->route('articles.index')
            ->with('success', 'Article deleted.');
    }
}

PHP Attributes NEW in Laravel 13

Laravel 13 introduces native PHP 8 attributes across 15+ locations, replacing traditional $property declarations. Fully optional and backward compatible.

Before (Laravel 12) — Properties
class Invoice extends Model
{
    protected $table = 'invoices';
    protected $primaryKey = 'invoice_id';
    protected $keyType = 'string';
    public $incrementing = false;
    protected $fillable = [
        'amount', 'status', 'user_id',
    ];
    protected $hidden = ['internal_notes'];
}

Eloquent ORM

Model

Article.php
namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsTo;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\BelongsToMany;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Relations\HasMany;

class Article extends Model
{
    protected $fillable = [
        'title', 'body', 'author_id', 'published',
    ];

    protected $casts = [
        'published' => 'boolean',
        'created_at' => 'datetime',
    ];

    // Accessor

    public function getExcerptAttribute(): string
    {
        return substr($this->body, 0, 150) . '...';
    }

    // Mutator

    public function setTitleAttribute(string $value): void
    {
        $this->attributes['title'] = trim($value);
    }

    // Relationships

    public function author(): BelongsTo
    {
        return $this->belongsTo(User::class, 'author_id');
    }

    public function tags(): BelongsToMany
    {
        return $this->belongsToMany(Tag::class);
    }

    public function comments(): HasMany
    {
        return $this->hasMany(Comment::class);
    }

    // Local scope

    public function scopePublished($query)
    {
        return $query->where('published', true);
    }

    public function scopeRecent($query)
    {
        return $query->orderBy('created_at', 'desc');
    }
}

Migration

use Illuminate\Database\Migrations\Migration;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Schema;

return new class extends Migration
{
    public function up(): void
    {
        Schema::create('articles', function (Blueprint $table) {
            $table->id();
            $table->string('title', 255);
            $table->text('body');
            $table->foreignId('author_id')
                ->constrained('users')->cascadeOnDelete();
            $table->boolean('published')->default(false);
            $table->timestamps();
            $table->softDeletes();
        });
    }

    public function down(): void
    {
        Schema::dropIfExists('articles');
    }
};

Validation

FormRequest — StoreArticleRequest.php
namespace App\Http\Requests;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Http\FormRequest;

class StoreArticleRequest extends FormRequest
{
    public function authorize(): bool
    {
        return true; // or Gate check

    }

    public function rules(): array
    {
        return [
            'title' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255', 'min:5'],
            'body' => ['required', 'string', 'min:50'],
            'author_id' => ['required', 'exists:users,id'],
            'published' => ['boolean'],
            'tags' => ['array'],
            'tags.*' => ['exists:tags,id'],
            'email' => ['required', 'email:rfc,dns'],
            'publish_date' => ['date', 'after:today'],
        ];
    }

    public function messages(): array
    {
        return [
            'title.required' => 'A title is required.',
            'body.min' => 'Body must be at least 50 characters.',
        ];
    }

    // After validation

    public function withValidator($validator): void
    {
        $validator->after(function ($validator) {
            if ($this->hasSpam($this->input('body'))) {
                $validator->errors()->add(
                    'body', 'Content contains spam.'
                );
            }
        });
    }
}

// In controller:

public function store(StoreArticleRequest $request)
{
    // $request->validated() returns validated data

    Article::create($request->validated());
}
Inline Validation in Controller
public function store(Request $request)
{
    $validated = $request->validate([
        'title' => 'required|string|max:255',
        'body' => 'required|string',
        'author_id' => 'required|exists:users,id',
        'published' => 'boolean',
    ]);

    Article::create($validated);
}

Sanctum — API Token Auth
// routes/api.php

Route::middleware('auth:sanctum')->get('/user',
    fn(Request $r) => $r->user()
);

// Issuing tokens

$token = $user->createToken('api-token')->plainTextToken;

// Login controller

public function login(Request $request)
{
    $credentials = $request->validate([
        'email' => 'required|email',
        'password' => 'required',
    ]);

    if (Auth::attempt($credentials)) {
        $token = $request->user()->createToken('api');
        return response()->json([
            'token' => $token->plainTextToken,
        ]);
    }

    return response()->json([
        'message' => 'Invalid credentials',
    ], 401);
}

Authorization

Policy — ArticlePolicy.php
namespace App\Policies;

use App\Models\Article;
use App\Models\User;

class ArticlePolicy
{
    public function viewAny(?User $user): bool
    {
        return true;
    }

    public function view(?User $user, Article $article): bool
    {
        return true; // public articles

    }

    public function create(User $user): bool
    {
        return true; // any authenticated user

    }

    public function update(User $user, Article $article): bool
    {
        return $user->id === $article->author_id;
    }

    public function delete(User $user, Article $article): bool
    {
        return $this->update($user, $article);
    }
}

// Register in AuthServiceProvider:

protected $policies = [
    Article::class => ArticlePolicy::class,
];

Queue / Job System

Laravel provides a unified queue API across many backends. Use Horizon for Redis-powered dashboards.

1. Create a Job

app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmail.php
namespace App\Jobs;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable;
use Illuminate\Queue\Attributes\Job; // Laravel 13


#[Job(queue: 'emails', tries: 3, backoff: 30)]
class SendWelcomeEmail implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Queueable;

    public function __construct(
        public User $user
    ) {}

    public function handle(): void
    {
        // Send email

        Mail::to($this->user->email)
            ->send(new WelcomeMail($this->user));
    }
}

2. Dispatch Jobs

// Simple dispatch

SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user);

// With delay

SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user)->delay(now()->addMinutes(10));

// On a specific queue

SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user)->onQueue('emails');

// Job chains (sequential)

Bus::chain([
    new ProcessPodcast($podcast),
    new OptimizePodcast($podcast),
    new SendNotification($podcast),
])->dispatch();

// Job batches

Bus::batch([
    new ProcessFile($file1),
    new ProcessFile($file2),
])->then(function () {
    // All jobs complete

})->dispatch();

// From controller:

public function register(Request $request)
{
    $user = User::create($request->validated());
    SendWelcomeEmail::dispatch($user);
    return redirect()->home();
}

3. Run the Worker

Worker Commands
# Start queue worker (processes jobs)

php artisan queue:work

# With specific queue and options

php artisan queue:work redis \
    --queue=high,default,low \
    --max-jobs=100 \
    --max-time=3600 \
    --memory=256 \
    --tries=3 \
    --backoff=30 \
    --sleep=3

# Start Horizon (dashboard at /horizon)

php artisan horizon

# Supervisor config (production)

[program:laravel-worker]
process_name=%(program_name)s_%(process_num)02d
command=php /var/www/artisan queue:work redis --sleep=3 --tries=3
autostart=true
autorestart=true
numprocs=4
user=forge

4. Failed Jobs

# Table for failed jobs

php artisan queue:failed-table
php artisan migrate

# Forget a single failed job

# Delete all failed jobs

API Resource Controller
namespace App\Http\Controllers\Api;

use App\Models\Article;
use App\Http\Resources\ArticleResource;
use App\Http\Requests\StoreArticleRequest;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;

class ArticleController extends Controller
{
    public function index(): JsonResponse
    {
        $articles = Article::with('author', 'tags')
            ->latest()
            ->paginate(20);

        return ArticleResource::collection($articles)
            ->response();
    }

    public function show(Article $article): JsonResponse
    {
        $article->load('author', 'tags');
        return (new ArticleResource($article))
            ->response();
    }

    public function store(StoreArticleRequest $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $article = auth()->user()->articles()
            ->create($request->validated());

        return (new ArticleResource($article))
            ->response()
            ->setStatusCode(201);
    }

    public function update(UpdateArticleRequest $request, Article $article): JsonResponse
    {
        $article->update($request->validated());
        return (new ArticleResource($article))->response();
    }

    public function destroy(Article $article): JsonResponse
    {
        $article->delete();
        return response()->json([
            'message' => 'Deleted',
        ], 200);
    }
}

namespace App\Http\Resources;

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Http\Resources\Json\JsonResource;

class ArticleResource extends JsonResource
{
    public function toArray(Request $request): array
    {
        return [
            'id' => $this->id,
            'title' => $this->title,
            'body' => $this->body,
            'excerpt' => $this->excerpt,
            'published' => $this->published,
            'author' => new UserResource($this->whenLoaded('author')),
            'tags' => TagResource::collection($this->whenLoaded('tags')),
            'created_at' => $this->created_at,
            'updated_at' => $this->updated_at,
        ];
    }
}

Middleware

Custom Middleware — CorsMiddleware.php
namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class CorsMiddleware
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        $response = $next($request);

        $response->headers->set('Access-Control-Allow-Origin', '*');
        $response->headers->set(
            'Access-Control-Allow-Headers',
            'X-Requested-With, Content-Type, Authorization'
        );
        $response->headers->set(
            'Access-Control-Allow-Methods',
            'GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS'
        );

        return $response;
    }
}

Testing

Laravel supports PHPUnit and Pest. Tests live in tests/. Run with php artisan test.

Model Factory
// database/factories/ArticleFactory.php

namespace Database\Factories;

use App\Models\Article;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory;

class ArticleFactory extends Factory
{
    protected $model = Article::class;

    public function definition(): array
    {
        return [
            'title' => fake()->sentence(),
            'body' => fake()->paragraphs(3, true),
            'author_id' => User::factory(),
            'published' => fake()->boolean(),
        ];
    }

    public function published(): static
    {
        return $this->state(['published' => true]);
    }
}
Feature Test
namespace Tests\Feature;

use App\Models\Article;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Tests\TestCase;

class ArticleTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    public function test_articles_list_can_be_rendered(): void
    {
        Article::factory()->count(3)->published()->create();

        $response = $this->get('/articles');

        $response->assertOk();
        $response->assertSee('Articles');
    }

    public function test_authenticated_user_can_create_article(): void
    {
        $user = User::factory()->create();

        $response = $this->actingAs($user)->post('/articles', [
            'title' => 'Test Article',
            'body' => 'Content for the test article.',
            'published' => true,
        ]);

        $response->assertRedirect();
        $this->assertDatabaseHas('articles', [
            'title' => 'Test Article',
            'author_id' => $user->id,
        ]);
    }

    public function test_unauthenticated_user_cannot_create(): void
    {
        $response = $this->postJson('/api/articles', [
            'title' => 'Test',
            'body' => 'Content',
        ]);

        $response->assertUnauthorized();
    }
}

// Run: php artisan test

Best Practices

Laravel Naming Conventions — Models: singular PascalCase (Article). Tables: plural snake_case (articles). Controllers: singular PascalCase (ArticleController). Migrations: descriptive (create_articles_table). Foreign keys: singular author_id. Pivot tables: alphabetical singular (article_tag). Routes: kebab-case (/api/articles/{slug}).
Recommended Practices
  • Use Eloquent, avoid raw SQL
  • Eager load with with()
  • Use FormRequest for validation
  • Skinny controllers, fat models
  • Use policies for authorization
  • Queue long-running tasks
  • Write tests for all features
  • Use env() only in config files
  • Cache config/routes in production
  • Never .env in version control
